ShipGremlins / early alpha

Your local operator guide.

Adopt a PM Gremlin and give it a useful job. Review its findings, test the changes, and track delivery through production.

Bring an idea to review a new crew and its private-by-default repository, then approve the foundation build. For an existing app, adopt one PM with a focused product brief and try one assignment with automation paused. Browser setup can wait until there is an app to explore.

This page is a static reference. Open the management dashboard with gremlins setup to connect tools, add an app, and create a local Docker worker. No fork, automation repository, or CI runner is required.

Give your gremlins a home

npm install -g git+https://github.com/AgentBurgundy/shipgremlins.git
gremlins setup

# Homelab: open the printed private link on another device
gremlins setup --lan

# Keep the controller running after closing the terminal
gremlins start --lan --port 4311
gremlins status
gremlins stop

Local workers use Claude Code and Playwright MCP with GitHub or GitLab source repositories, Linear tickets, and optional browser targets. Use repository checks, a direct URL, or Vercel, Railway, or Cloud Run discovery. A worker becomes Ready after a real Chromium screenshot check. Other AI runtimes, provider provisioning, and automatic local production promotion remain planned. Existing GitHub Actions and GCE setups remain advanced options.

Done means merged into production

gremlins tickets audit --project my-app --json

Audit is read-only. Completion requires a reviewed finite deliverable manifest and explicit apply. Staging and verification alone do not close a ticket.

Local developers run configured checks before opening draft PRs or merge requests to the selected base branch. They never mark tickets Done or merge into production.
